newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Petronas says in storage terminal joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Petronas says in storage terminal joint venture.

text.p: Malaysian national oil firm Petronas said on Monday it has signed a joint venture agreement with GATX Terminals (Pte) Ltd and Dialog MCV Sdn Bhd to build a 300 million ringgit bulk chemical storage terminal in eastern Terengganu state.
Petronas said in a statement that it will hold a 40 percent stake in the joint venture company, with GATX and Dialog MCV each holding a 30 percent stake.
The terminal is expected to have an annual volume throughput of about 2.7 million metric tonnes.
It will be built in phases over two years with initial operations scheduled for the third quarter of 1999, the statement said. Full operation is expected in 2000.
GATX Terminals is an associate company of U.S.-based GATX Terminals Corp, while Dialog MCV is a partnership between Malaysia's Dialog Group Bhd and Malaysian Capital Ventures Sdn Bhd.
The shareholders' agreement signed on Monday is the result of a feasibility study undertaken following the signing of a letter of intent last July for the project, Petronas said.

The terminal will provide centralised services for the handling, storage and distribution of chemical and petrochemical feedstocks, products and by-products to Petronas' joint venture petrochemical plants as well as other customers around the Kampung Tok Arun and Kertih areas in Malaysia.
